title: Blackstone Steak Sandwiches
shortDescription: Au jus dip energy without the fuss
subtitle: Au jus dip energy without the fuss
description: Canadian hall legend. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Season and temper
steps.instruction: Pat steaks dry. Salt heavily 40 minutes ahead (or right before if rushed). Pepper just before cooking. Let meat sit out 20 minutes — cold centers overcook the exterior.

steps.title: Grill over high heat
steps.instruction: Grill over high heat (450–500°F surface) 3–5 minutes per side for strip to 130°F medium-rare. Flank: sear 4 minutes per side, then medium until 125°F; rest and slice thin against the grain.

steps.title: Baste with herb butter
steps.instruction: Melt butter with garlic and parsley. Rest steaks 8 minutes tented with foil, then slice and spoon butter over. Hold on warm trays at 180°F no more than 20 minutes.

steps.title: Serve on sheet trays
steps.instruction: Blackstone Steak Sandwiches goes out sliced on trays with extra herb butter melting on top — crew grabs with tongs, not forks and knives.

proTips: Warm rolls before building — cold bread kills the line.
Serve jus in mugs for easy dipping.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Blackstone Steak Sandwiches with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Blackstone Steak Sandwiches on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Au jus dip energy without the fuss. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
